question: In chlorine disinfection, which two factors are combined in the CT concept used to judge disinfection performance?
correctAnswer: Residual chlorine concentration and contact time
explanation: CT combines the residual chlorine concentration with the time the water is in contact with it, so both factors shape disinfection performance.
options: Effluent flow rate and contact basin water depth
Residual chlorine concentration and contact time
Water temperature and ultraviolet lamp operating age
Chlorine storage volume and sludge blanket depth
sourceTitle: US EPA: Municipal Wastewater — supporting treatment resources
sourceReference: Supporting resource category: Advanced Effluent Disinfection. See SOURCES.md: these are not claim-level verification citations.
optionA: Effluent flow rate and contact basin water depth
optionB: Residual chlorine concentration and contact time
optionC: Water temperature and ultraviolet lamp operating age
optionD: Chlorine storage volume and sludge blanket depth

question: When operators track volatile solids reduction across a digester, what does the reduction figure describe?
correctAnswer: The share of incoming volatile solids destroyed in digestion
explanation: Volatile solids reduction compares the volatile solids fed to the digester with those destroyed, showing how much organic material digestion converted.
options: The share of grit removed in the headworks channels
The share of scum skimmed from the primary clarifiers
The share of incoming volatile solids destroyed in digestion
The share of water evaporated from the sludge holding tank

question: What is the main biological process that reduces volatile solids inside an aerobic digester?
correctAnswer: Endogenous respiration of the biomass held in the tank
explanation: In aerobic digestion the biomass consumes its own cell material for energy, a process called endogenous respiration, which lowers the volatile solids content.
options: Endogenous respiration of the biomass held in the tank
Methane fermentation by anaerobic organisms in the tank
Chemical precipitation of phosphorus in the tank contents
Settling and compaction of solids at the tank bottom

optionD: Settling and compaction of solids at the tank bottom

The polymer share of the conditioning chemical solution
The grit share of the solids captured by the screens

Dry tonnes change whenever the cake storage pad is cleaned

To increase the chemical residual left in the effluent after disinfection

To settle suspended solids before the effluent leaves the disinfection unit

Increase the feed loading to push gas production back up
Drain the digester contents and restart it with fresh seed
Stop all heating so the digester cools toward ambient levels

Longer channel travel time giving the water too much exposure

Aeration strips alkalinity out of the sludge along with the air

Settling concentrates alkalinity in the supernatant layer drawn off

Energy is wasted overcoming the restriction the valve creates

Ammonia coats the contact tank walls so chlorine cannot mix in

question: An aerobic digester nitrifies strongly and its pH has fallen low enough to slow digestion. Which response best protects the process?
correctAnswer: Add alkalinity or blend the feed to restore buffering capacity
explanation: Restoring alkalinity, directly or by blending feed, rebuilds the buffering capacity that nitrification consumed and lets digestion recover at a workable pH.
options: Stop all aeration for a week so the nitrifying organisms die off
Raise the feed rate sharply so fresh sludge dilutes the nitrifiers
Add alkalinity or blend the feed to restore buffering capacity
Draw off the digester contents and refill it with primary effluent
